full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the appeal in brief are that the plaintiff joined the Government service as an Inspector of Co-operative Societies in 1950 and while posted at Dinajpur he was not pulling on well with his superior Officer, defendant No. 3 who managed to obtain an order of plaintiff's transfer to Setabganj. The plaintiff submitted a representation to respondent No. 2 for cancellation of the order of transfer but did not receive any reply to his representation for cancellation of the transfer order. Thereafter, he was put under suspension by respondent No. 2. 12 charges were framed against him and the Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Societies was appointed as the Enquiry Officer. The plaintiff was, however, found guilty on 5 out of 12 charges by the Enquiry Officer who in his report recommended admonition and severe warning as penalty. But respondent No. 2 did not accept the said recommendation and asked the plaintiff to show-cause as to why he should not be dismissed from service. After the plaintiff had show-cause the respondent No. 2 passed an order removing the plaintiff from his service with effect from the date of his suspension, Hence the present suit. The defendants contested the suit by filing a joint written statement in which they denied the material allegations made in the plaint and assorted that the order of removal of the plaintiff from his service was quite legal and has been passed in accordance with law.
